pattern.top_pattern: CA nursing facility and SNF rare-case concentration
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA / NF and SNF - FREE STANDING / LTSS Non Dual
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC

impact_summary.volume_signal: claims up from a low base

pattern.pattern_details: CA NF spend is being pushed by a cluster of rare diagnoses, and the same market also shows added SNF pressure in LTSS Non Dual. The NF signal is concentrated in feeding tube or ostomy, digestive, and connective tissue diagnoses, while SNF spend is concentrated in digestive and connective tissue DRGs. Together this points to a post-acute and nursing-facility management issue in CA rather than a broad statewide trend.
pattern.why_it_matters: Post-acute concentration can drive avoidable spend through placement, length-of-stay, and payment-rule leakage if not addressed early.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run a CA post-acute review that links NF episodes to SNF utilization for the flagged diagnoses, and verify whether placement, length of stay, and SNF payment rules were appropriate.
pattern.validation_reason: The signal comes from low-baseline rare cases, and the operational and clinical views may overlap, so claim-level linkage is needed before sizing broad intervention.
evidence_summary: CA NF rare cases totaled about $180K, led by M069 at about $69K on 3 claims and Z431 at about $37K on 10 claims.
Additional CA NF diagnoses M359, K9423, and K611 added about $75K combined.
CA LTSS Non Dual / SNF - FREE STANDING added about $54K, concentrated in Other Digestive System Diagnoses without CC/MCC and Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC.
